description:
Acquire the cooperative lock only for the smallest critical section that directly controls transient, globally shared Unity Editor state, or whose state-sensitive tool calls require that state to remain unchanged. Examples are changing Play/Pause/Edit Mode, explicitly starting compilation or a domain reload, switching the active scene or Prefab Stage, changing Selection, or focusing Editor windows. Acquire at the last possible moment, immediately before the first state-control call; release immediately after the last state-dependent call with `unity_release`. Never hold the lock for an entire task or workflow.

Asset and code work does not require this lock. Keep preparation, searches, reads, writes, creation, deletion, imports, and ordinary verification of scripts, animation clips, controllers, prefabs, scenes, ScriptableObjects, and other assets outside the critical section when they target explicit paths, GUIDs, or objects. This remains true when those changes may cause a later import or compilation. If a workflow explicitly calls `unity_recompile`, only the recompile/state-dependent portion may need the lock; the code edits before it and asset verification after it remain outside.

The decision is based only on direct shared Editor-state interference, not on whether an operation mutates assets or on `unity_execute.readonly`. A mutating `unity_execute` runs without this lock when it targets explicit objects or paths and does not control or depend on transient Editor state. Read-only queries and safe background work are additional lock-free cases. This is a cooperative protocol: Unity tools remain callable without the lock.

`mode: "wait"` waits in FIFO order until acquisition, cancellation, or timeout. `mode: "try"` first reclaims a holder whose session is no longer running, then returns immediately with `status=busy` when an active session still owns the lock so other asynchronous work can continue. A busy result is an expected, non-error outcome and reports the complete holder session and reason. Try mode respects existing waiters and does not jump the queue. Repeated acquisition by the current owner is idempotent.

reason.description: Short description of only the direct Editor-state control or dependency inside this minimal critical section, shown to Agents waiting for the lock. Do not list asset or code edits.

mode.description: Acquisition behavior. `wait` queues until the lock is acquired; `try` returns immediately when an active session owns the lock or another session is already queued.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum time to wait for the cooperative lock. Defaults to 300 seconds.
